Description: **PK.** Unique identifier for a listing, also referred to as listing_id. You can view any live listing at https://ebay.com/itm/{item_id}.
Site where the item is listed. Common values: 0=US, 3=UK, 15=AU, 77=eBay Motors, 100=eBay.com (2nd channel). Always filter on this field — tables are partitioned by it.
Generated sequence tracking revisions made by the seller. Increments on each significant update.
Timestamp when the listing record was first created. Note: use auct_start_dt as the listing go-live date, not this field.
Timestamp of the last modification to this listing. Read-only.
UUID tag used by sellers or API clients to ensure idempotent listing creation (prevents duplicate listings).
Identifier of the application used to create the listing (e.g., SYI tool, third-party API client).
Client IP address from which the listing was created.
Item title as it appears in search results and on the listing page.
Full subtitle text. Null if not provided by seller.
True if seller opted for boldface title display (paid listing upgrade).
Listing format code. Common values: 1=Chinese Auction (with or without BIN), 2=Dutch Auction, 7=Store Fixed Price, 9=Fixed Price, 13=Classified Ad. -999=Unknown.
Activity status of the listing. Values: 0=Live (may still be on-hold; check onhold flag), 1=Ended, 2=Admin Ended (by CS), 3=Deleted, 4=Scheduled.
Date the listing went live. Use this as the listing start date — scheduled listings exist in the table before going live, so site_create_date is not equivalent.
Date the listing ended or is scheduled to end. For GTC listings, this rolls forward every 30 days. Use this field for partition-filtered queries.
Timestamp (with time) of listing start. See auct_start_dt for date-only queries.
Timestamp (with time) of listing end. Daylight Saving Time may cause minor offsets vs site timestamps.
Date the listing was originally scheduled to end (set at creation; not updated if listing ends early). Archived items show 1969-12-31; half listings show far-future dates.
Code identifying why the listing ended (e.g., sold, expired, admin-ended).
Number of items in a lot. A lot contains two or more similar items sold together as a single order line.
True if listing is private — buyer user IDs are hidden from the listing and bid history.
Number of significant revisions made to this listing by the seller.
Current quantity available for sale (initial quantity minus quantity sold).
Total quantity sold from this listing.
True if the seller has specified a return policy for this listing.
Item ID of the parent listing if this listing was created via Relist, Sell Similar, or Bulk Relist.
Item ID of the new listing if this item has been relisted. Greater than 0 means this listing ended and a successor was created.
Foreign key into EBAY_PRODUCT (ePID) to retrieve catalog-level product information.
Start timestamp of a promotional sale applied to this listing.
End timestamp of a promotional sale applied to this listing.
Number of images uploaded for this listing.
Photo display mode. Values: 0=None, 1=Gallery, 2=Featured, 7=Gallery Plus.
Semicolon-delimited list of all image URLs for this listing.
URL of the thumbnail image shown in search results (usually the first image).
Gallery image type indicator for the gallery_url image.
Seller-provided item location (city, state, country text).
Country ID where the item is physically located (seller-declared).
Postal code of the seller's address.
True if the listing used the Super Featured paid listing upgrade.
